newsitem.title: UK: Clyde says "wait and see" on incentives.
newsitem.headline: Clyde says "wait and see" on incentives.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc said on Monday that shareholders hoping for incentives to stick with the company rather than accept a hostile bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd should "wait and see".

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Group Managing Director Roy Franklin said Clyde would publish "a very robust defence" against Gulf Canada's bid in early January. Clyde is obliged to publish its defence by the end of next week.
Franklin declined to say if the document would include incentives for shareholders, saying "the answer has to be wait and see".

On Wednesday Gulf Canada said it planned to offer Clyde shareholders 105 pence per share in cash in a debt-funded hostile bid which valued the British oil and gas explorer and producer at 432 million stg.
Clyde shares were down 1/2p at 117 pence in early afternoon trade on Monday.
British analysts believe any counter-offer for the group would have to be pitched at around 120 pence per share to succeed.

Franklin, who dismissed the Gulf Canada bid as "opportunistic", said: "There is and will be a very robust defence. I believe we can offer our shareholders value over the course of time substantially better than this offer."

He said Clyde had spoken to its major shareholders about the bid. "They have followed us over the last three years and seen what has been achieved, and will wait to see how the debate develops," he added.
The group managing director also said the emergence of a bid for the company had not come as a complete surprise.

"I didn't feel that our rating in the UK market reflected the performance of the comapny over the past three years and on that basis there was always the risk of a bid. But it gives us the opportunity to set out our case to shareholders," he said.
